Sample Name: Primary Care Followup and Preventive Screening
Description: Hypertension, prior substance use, foot complaints, and requests for preventive and infectious disease screening.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 55-year-old man presents for followup after a recent hospitalization and describes substantial improvement in his general condition. He is living in a recovery residence and working with social services to secure stable housing. He reports abstinence from prior cocaine and heroin use, with alcohol identified as a trigger for relapse. He continues to smoke approximately one-half pack per day and is interested in cessation. Nicotine gum has helped briefly in the past. He requests HIV testing and agrees to hepatitis B screening in the setting of a history of hepatitis C. He has painful corns and calluses of the feet, with inadequate response to the topical preparation supplied previously. He states that he has been taking lisinopril 10 mg daily, by splitting 20 mg tablets, as instructed. He requests colorectal screening, having had a prior rectal examination but no confirmed colonoscopy. He denies medication allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY: Resides in a recovery home and is seeking independent housing. History of substance use, now reporting abstinence. Current tobacco use.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Cardiac rhythm was regular on auscultation. Examination of the lungs and abdomen was performed without a new major abnormality described.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Hypertension. Continue prescribed lisinopril and monitor blood pressure.
2. Prior substance use disorder. Encouraged continued recovery activities and social service support. Tobacco cessation methods were reviewed.
3. Infectious disease screening. HIV and hepatitis B testing were requested; the patient was advised that results require in-person discussion and that counseling is available.
4. Foot calluses and skin complaints. Podiatry referral and an alternative topical treatment were arranged.
5. Health maintenance. Colonoscopy referral and fasting lipid testing were requested.
Return for test results as directed and for routine followup in six months.
